mathematics_checks: Induct on prefix length: if Q gives positive mass to (h,x), then Q(h)>0 and q_t(x|h)>0; the induction hypothesis and conditional support give P(h)>0 and p_t(x|h)>0. Thus the ratios L_t are genuine finite-prefix densities even on P-null histories, where both measures vanish. On a P-positive atom, summing q_t over the p_t-positive transitions gives 1, and expanding sum(q_t-p_t)^2/p_t gives sum q_t^2/p_t - 1. Consequently E_P[L_(t+1)|F_t]=L_t and E_P[L_(t+1)^2|F_t]=L_t^2(1+eta_t).

A_(t+1)=A_t(1+eta_t) is F_t-measurable, positive, and finite for finite t. Dividing the conditional square identity by it yields a mean-one nonnegative martingale L_t^2/A_t. The simultaneous pathwise bound gives log A_t<=sum_{s<t} eta_s<=B, hence E_P L_t^2<=e^B. Averaging eta_t under P cannot replace this predictable normalization: the square recursion weights histories by L_t^2.

For m>=n, E_P(L_m L_n)=E_P L_n^2 by conditional expectation, so the squared L2 distance equals the difference of the squared norms. The norms are monotone and bounded, giving a genuine L2 limit with a nonnegative measurable representative; convergence in L1 gives mean one. For any E in F_n, the integrals of L_m on E equal Q(E) for all m>=n. The union of the increasing F_n is an algebra generating the product sigma algebra, so equality of the probability measures Q and L P there gives equality on the entire space. Finite-prefix absolute continuity alone would not justify this step.

Because tau is canonical, {tau=infinity}=intersection_n {tau>n} is measurable and transfers as a P-null event once full-path absolute continuity has been proved. Common deterministic dummy continuation creates no new likelihood factor on stopped positive prefixes with the stated padding tables; a version on a Q-null prefix cannot create later Q mass. No deterministic time cap or Q-termination premise enters the proof. L and W lie in L2(P), so Cauchy-Schwarz first proves E_Q W=E_P[LW] finite (P-null infinite values are also Q-null). Then E_P L=1 gives E_P(L-1)^2=E_P L^2-1 and centering W gives exactly the stated variance estimate.

For the two-call family, p=m^-2 and q=m^-1 are both in (0,1), and both second outcomes are P-possible on the rare first-one branch. The first eta is (q-p)^2/[p(1-p)]=(m-1)/(m+1). On the rare branch the second eta is (1-p)^2/p+(1-p)=(1-p)/p=m^2-1; on the other branch and after the two calls it is zero. Thus the supremum of partial expected budgets is (m-1)/(m+1)+1-m^-2<2, although the pathwise budget on the P-positive rare branch grows with m.

The terminal event E={11} has masses P(E)=m^-4 and Q(E)=m^-1; W=m^2 times its indicator has E_P W=m^-2, E_P W^2=1 and E_Q W=m. In fact the only Q-positive two-bit prefixes are 11 and 00, so E_P L_2^2=m^2+(m-1)/(m+1), confirming the stated lower bound. The counterexample uses the expressly allowed terminal charge, not the raw count of two transitions; the premises do not impose a unit base cost on each active call. Even a fixed positive base charge in normalized units is possible: (1+W)/2 has ideal second moment (1+m^-2)/2<=1 and Q-mean (1+m)/2.

Valid alternatives such as the L2-bounded martingale convergence theorem followed by uniqueness on cylinders should receive the same credit; stopping and cost are not justified by a calculation confined to a finite prefix.

The third point requires valid conditional tables, the ideal average budget and work moments plus divergence, not the specific powers of m or counting raw calls as W. The last point independently scores the substantive applicability audit: identify conditional domination and a pathwise likelihood budget on common histories, and a second moment of actual total work under the reference law, without claiming either actual algorithm meets these conditions.

source_assumption_differences: The TV declaration accepts arbitrary measurable carriers and Markov kernels with integrable eventwise domination under a shared input law; it needs no conditional absolute continuity and asserts no likelihood bound. Even on a two-point space K=delta_0 and L=(1-epsilon)delta_0+epsilon delta_1 have event discrepancy at most epsilon for 0<epsilon<1 yet L is not dominated by K. A shared suffix bounds output events and does not retain or construct the full histories. The exercise instead adds one-sided q_t<<p_t at P-positive histories, canonical stopped binary paths, and a deterministic uniform bound on accumulated conditional chi-square under P.

The SPHMC theorem assumes a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, a finite node type, C2 potential with normalized Hessian bounds and supplied stationary xstar, 0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, nonnegative time and budget constants, an incoming state-square integral at most M, and supplied bounded nodes/rows. The binary exercise imports none of these or the full Gaussian phase law; it assumes P-a.s. stopping and a square-integrable actual total work observable instead. First count moments, even on every node of a phase, do not by themselves supply that stopped-work second moment, and the cited declaration has no pair of ideal/implemented history measures or density budget.

An actual application would require a common measurable encoding of the full execution (including stopping and padding), conditional Radon-Nikodym versions and an accumulated pathwise square budget, plus the correctly defined ideal total-work L2 estimate including any charge and aggregation across phases. If the natural histories are not the stated binary model, an appropriate extension or a justified encoding is also needed; small output TV or a common Gaussian drive alone is not that adapter.
